records.answer: Yes. Studio 17 can write short-form scripts around an audience, a clear message and the intended action. The script can include the opening hook, spoken copy, visual sequence and on-screen text. Filming and editing are separate unless included in the production scope.
searchTerms: can you write scripts for reels and tiktok ads

records.question: What is a hook in short-form video scripting?
records.answer: A hook is the opening that gives the intended viewer a reason to keep watching. It might show a recognisable problem, demonstrate a result or ask a relevant question. It should match what the video actually delivers, rather than attract attention with a misleading promise.
searchTerms: what is a hook in short-form video scripting

records.question: When should businesses use AI-generated marketing visuals?
records.answer: AI-generated visuals can suit concepts, stylised campaigns and ideas that would be impractical to photograph. Use real or carefully verified imagery when customers need an accurate view of a product, property or person. Review every asset for brand accuracy, misleading details and appropriate rights before publication.
searchTerms: when should businesses use ai-generated marketing visuals

records.question: How can brands maintain consistency with AI-generated content?
records.answer: Keep an approved visual reference for colours, typography, composition and the appearance of actual products. Review every AI-generated asset against those references and check for invented packaging, distorted details or misleading claims before publishing it.
searchTerms: brands maintain consistency with ai-generated content

records.question: What are the limitations of AI-generated product images?
records.answer: AI can invent product features, alter packaging, distort text or show materials inaccurately. These errors can mislead customers even when the image looks convincing. Compare generated images with approved product references and use real photography when accurate representation cannot be assured.
searchTerms: what are the limitations of ai-generated product images

records.question: Can Meta Ads generate qualified business leads?
records.answer: Meta lead campaigns can generate enquiries, but qualified leads depend on targeting, offer, form design and sales follow-up.
searchTerms: can meta ads generate qualified business leads

records.question: Should I run Google Search Ads or Performance Max?
records.answer: Search Ads capture stated intent; Performance Max runs across several Google surfaces with broader automation. Fit depends on goals and tracking.
searchTerms: should i run google search ads or performance max

records.question: What makes a good Google Ads landing page?
records.answer: A strong landing page matches the ad promise, explains the offer clearly and makes conversion easy on mobile.
searchTerms: what makes a good google ads landing page

records.question: How do you measure Google Ads return on investment?
records.answer: Compare attributable revenue or qualified pipeline value against total campaign costs; validate data quality before calculating ROI.
searchTerms: measure google ads return on investment

records.question: Which social media advertising platform is best for small businesses?
records.answer: Choose channels based on audience behaviour, buying stage, creative resources and whether customers are actively searching.
searchTerms: which social media advertising platform is best for small businesses

records.question: How do I choose creative formats for social ads?
records.answer: Match creative to placements and objectives: short vertical video for feeds, clear stills for simple offers, and testing for uncertainty.
searchTerms: choose creative formats for social ads

records.question: Why are my social ads getting clicks but no enquiries?
records.answer: Clicks without enquiries may reflect mismatched targeting, misleading creative, slow pages or unclear offers. Review the full journey.
searchTerms: my social ads getting clicks but no enquiries

records.question: How do influencer advertising campaigns work?
records.answer: Influencer advertising starts with choosing a creator whose audience matches the product and agreeing on a brief, deliverables and usage rights. The creator produces sponsored content, which can be published on their account, licensed for paid ads or both. Campaigns should include disclosure requirements, approval steps and measurement such as qualified visits or sales, not follower count alone.
searchTerms: influencer advertising campaigns work

records.question: How should I choose an influencer for my brand?
records.answer: Assess audience relevance, credibility, engagement quality and commercial fit rather than follower counts alone.
searchTerms: choose an influencer for my brand

records.question: How can I measure influencer campaign performance?
records.answer: Track reach, visits, referral codes, qualified leads and sales where measurable; distinguish exposure from direct conversions.
searchTerms: measure influencer campaign performance

records.question: What is UGC content in marketing?
records.answer: User-generated content originally means material people create about a brand or experience, such as customer photos and reviews. Paid UGC creators also produce content in a similar personal style for a brand to use. Commissioned creator content should not be presented as an independent customer review.
searchTerms: what is ugc content in marketing

records.question: How is UGC different from influencer marketing?
records.answer: UGC refers to the content style or source; influencer marketing leverages a creator's audience and reach. They can overlap.
searchTerms: how is ugc different from influencer marketing

records.question: Can UGC videos be used in paid advertising?
records.answer: UGC videos can be used in ads if you have appropriate usage rights and advertising disclosures.
searchTerms: can ugc videos be used in paid advertising

records.question: What is the difference between email advertising and email marketing?
records.answer: Email advertising can refer to paid placements in others' newsletters; email marketing covers campaigns to your own permission-based list.
searchTerms: email advertising and email marketing

records.question: What makes an effective promotional email campaign?
records.answer: Relevant segmentation, a clear offer, readable design and strong deliverability practices improve email campaign quality.
searchTerms: what makes an effective promotional email campaign

records.question: What is brand identity and why does it matter?
records.answer: Brand identity is how people recognise your business across your website, social media, advertising and documents. It brings together the logo, colours, typography, imagery and tone of voice. A consistent identity makes even a small business look more established and easier to remember.
searchTerms: brand identity and why does it matter

records.question: What is a brand strategy for small businesses?
records.answer: A small business needs to know who it serves, why customers should choose it and what it wants to be known for. Brand strategy turns those decisions into consistent positioning, messaging and creative choices so marketing is recognisable rather than improvised.
searchTerms: a brand strategy for small businesses

records.question: How do I define my target audience and value proposition?
records.answer: Look at your best customers, the problems they need solved, their budget and why they choose you over alternatives. Your value proposition should state the audience, specific outcome and a credible reason to believe you—not just claim that your business is the best.
searchTerms: define my target audience and value proposition

records.question: What is the difference between branding and marketing?
records.answer: Branding defines what a business stands for and how customers recognise it. Marketing brings that message to people through content, advertising, search and other channels. You need both: more exposure won't help much if customers cannot understand what makes the business different.
searchTerms: branding and marketing

records.question: What makes a good business logo?
records.answer: A good logo works at small sizes, in one colour and across different formats. Distinctive type or symbols matter more than decoration; the final assets should include suitable versions for websites, social profiles and documents.
searchTerms: what makes a good business logo

records.question: Should a logo work in black and white?
records.answer: Yes. A logo should remain recognisable in black and white because it may appear on invoices, packaging, uniforms, documents or single-colour print. Colour is part of the identity, but the shape and lettering should still work without it.
searchTerms: should a logo work in black and white

records.question: Why does a company need a brand style guide?
records.answer: Without guidelines, different designers, staff and suppliers may use different fonts, logo versions and colours. A practical style guide reduces that inconsistency and helps campaigns, presentations, websites and printed materials look like one business.
searchTerms: a company need a brand style guide

records.question: When should a business consider rebranding?
records.answer: Consider rebranding when your business has changed audience, offer or positioning, or when the current identity no longer reflects the company. Start with a brand review; sometimes a clearer message and refreshed assets are enough without replacing everything.
searchTerms: consider rebranding

records.question: Can I rebrand without confusing existing customers?
records.answer: Yes, if the transition is planned. Keep useful recognisable elements, explain the change and update your website, social channels, email templates and customer touchpoints consistently. Customers should still recognise the business they already trust.
searchTerms: rebrand without confusing existing customers

records.question: How should a new brand identity be launched?
records.answer: A launch should coordinate the new logo and guidelines with updated website pages, social profiles, advertising assets, email signatures and key customer materials. Announce what changed and why, then check for old branding that may still be visible online.
searchTerms: a new brand identity be launched

records.question: How do I position my business against competitors?
records.answer: Positioning starts with the alternatives your customers are considering. Identify your audience, their most important need and a difference you can prove—such as a particular specialism, service model or outcome. Your website and campaigns should communicate that difference consistently.
searchTerms: position my business against competitors

records.question: What is a brand positioning statement?
records.answer: A positioning statement identifies who a brand serves, what category it competes in, the main customer benefit and why that claim is credible. It's a working decision tool for your website, advertising and sales messaging rather than necessarily a public slogan.
searchTerms: a brand positioning statement

records.question: How can brand positioning help premium pricing?
records.answer: Customers pay more when they understand meaningful differences in quality, expertise, convenience or service. Positioning helps explain those differences with evidence and reduces the temptation to compete only on discounts. It cannot justify a premium without real value.
searchTerms: brand positioning help premium pricing

records.question: What is brand tone of voice?
records.answer: Tone of voice describes how a brand sounds across its website, ads, captions and customer messages. Document clear word choices and examples, while allowing the level of formality to change by channel.
searchTerms: brand tone of voice

records.question: How do I keep a consistent brand message on every platform?
records.answer: Define a few core messages, proof points, vocabulary rules and examples for different channels. A LinkedIn post can sound more professional than a Reel, but the underlying promise and brand personality should stay consistent. Reusable copy guidelines help different team members achieve this.
searchTerms: keep a consistent brand message on every platform

records.question: What is the difference between brand messaging and copywriting?
records.answer: Brand messaging decides what your business needs to communicate—who it helps, the value it offers and why to believe it. Copywriting turns that strategy into actual website headlines, ads, emails and social captions tailored to each audience and action.
searchTerms: brand messaging and copywriting
